heading: INT. ST. CECILIA'S HOSPITAL - ROOFTOP GREENHOUSE OPERATING SUITE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. ST. CECILIA'S HOSPITAL - ROOFTOP GREENHOUSE OPERATING SUITE - NIGHT
Rain ticks on glass panels.
Ferns crowd the corners of a sterile field under the stars.
DR. MARGUERITE VOSS, fifties, silver braid tucked under her cap, hums as she sutures.
Across the table NURSE TOBIAS KANE, calm and broad, passes her instruments before she asks.
RESIDENT PRIYA NAIR, twenties, watches the monitor with a small smile.
Lovely tissue. Textbook.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: Pressure's a rock.
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: DR. HAL BRODERICK, the anesthesiologist, sixties, sips tea at his station and turns a crossword page.
SCRUB TECH JUNE ALVARADO counts sponges aloud, relaxed, almost singing it.
Eleven, twelve, thirteen.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: Fourteen is on the floor.
units.name: PRIYA

units.text: Then it's not in the patient. Wonderful.
units.name: VOSS

units.text: She ties off the last stitch.
Everyone exhales.
Tobias reaches for the dressing.
The greenhouse door hisses open.
DR. ANSELM FAIRWEATHER, hospital chief of surgery, steps in dripping, his mask on crooked.
He does not look at the patient.
He looks at Voss, and at the clipboard in his hand.
Broderick's pen stops moving over the crossword.
Tobias lowers the dressing, slowly, back to the tray.
June stops counting.
Dr. Voss. A word. Outside.
units.name: ANSELM

units.text: Voss sets down the needle driver, aligns it with the edge of the tray, and does not turn around.
